data.title: Sandbox
data.tagline: An isolated execution environment restricting the files, network, and system resources accessible by untrusted code or automated tasks.
data.learningOutcome: You can distinguish technical isolation from permission approval and read-only controls, and keep sensitive data out of the sandbox.
data.description: For example, an AI tool may let commands write only inside the current workspace and restrict network access, reducing the chance that a bad script affects unrelated files. A sandbox may use OS controls, containers, or virtual machines, and its strength depends on the actual boundary. Mounted sensitive folders, injected real keys, and allowed networks remain accessible to code inside it.

learning.assumes: You know that code or packages can execute local commands.
learning.outcome: You can distinguish technical isolation from permission approval and read-only controls, and keep sensitive data out of the sandbox.

distinctions.label: Permission Mode
distinctions.explanation: A Sandbox enforces execution containment at the system boundary; a Permission Mode dictates when to pause and prompt the user for approval.

explanation.title: Provide a restricted runtime
explanation.text: Code runs under OS sandbox controls, in a container, or in a virtual machine with limited files, processes, and network access.

explanation.title: Reduce host impact
explanation.text: A poisoned dependency or bad command is less able to read or modify sensitive host files even if it damages the sandbox.

explanation.title: Limit inputs first
explanation.text: Mount only what is needed, use mock data, and control the network instead of passing production credentials into the sandbox.

data.boundary: The sandbox determines what commands can access, the approval policy determines when they pause to ask, and read-only is one possible write boundary. A sandbox cannot protect data you deliberately mount or inject; if network access is allowed, code may still send that data elsewhere.

lessonPractice.title: Which setup combines sandbox isolation with least privilege when the AI debugs a database?

options.label: Run in a sandbox with only the needed code mounted and a test or mock data connection
options.feedback: Correct. The restricted environment and non-production data reduce exposure of the host, real database, and credentials.

options.label: Pass production database admin credentials into the sandbox because containers protect all data automatically
options.feedback: A sandbox cannot make intentionally injected production credentials safe; code may still use or exfiltrate them.

options.label: Set permission mode to allow and use that instead of environment isolation
options.feedback: Allow is an approval policy, not technical isolation; auto-running commands can increase host risk.

data.agentPrompt: Prepare an isolated environment for the test code with only the project code/ directory mounted and a mock data connection. State the file and network boundaries; do not inject production keys or database credentials.
